title: Tyres, Lights & Vehicle Condition
whatItIs: A car must be roadworthy every time it's used: legal tyres, clean working lights and, from 3 years old, a valid MOT.

keyFacts.text: Car tyres MUST have at least 1.6 mm of tread across the central 3/4 of the breadth, all the way round.
Tyres MUST be inflated to the manufacturer's specification for the load being carried.
Lights, indicators, reflectors and number plates MUST be kept clean and clear.
You MUST NOT drive without an MOT when one is needed, except to a pre-arranged test or to repairs for it.

keyFacts: Uneven tyre wear can mean faults in the brakes or suspension, or wheels out of alignment.

onTheTest.question: Your car pulls to one side when you brake. What is the most likely cause?
options: A brake fault or wrongly inflated tyres
onTheTest.why: Highway Code annex 6: pulling to one side when braking is most likely a brake fault or incorrectly inflated tyres.

onTheTest.question: A car failed its MOT with a 'dangerous' problem. What can happen if it's driven before repair?
options: A fine of up to £2,500, a ban and 3 points
Nothing while the old MOT is valid
onTheTest.why: GOV.UK: you can be fined up to £2,500, banned and get 3 penalty points for driving a vehicle that failed its MOT with a 'dangerous' problem.

traps: 1 mm is for motorcycles and large vehicles. For cars it's 1.6 mm.
Check pressures cold: warm tyres can give a misleading reading.
Car keeps bouncing after you push down on it? Worn shock absorbers.
